claim: With an exact or executable checker, sampling many candidates and filtering raises solve rate with no plateau up to thousands of samples (coverage grows roughly log-linearly). With a vote or a learned reward model as selector, gains stop near 100 samples even when coverage is above 95%.
agent_test: On an item set with a code checker, compare N=4,8,16 checked samples vs N voted samples at equal total tokens; record the gap between oracle coverage and selected accuracy. All lines trace to one paper (Brown 2024); Cobbe 2021 and Stroebl 2024 support the direction only.

claim: Best-of-N against a learned verifier is not monotone: accuracy peaks at a finite N and then falls because search finds answers that fool the verifier. Cobbe: peak near 400 completions for a 6B verifier. Gao: proxy-optimised gold reward rises then falls in both best-of-n and RL. Snell: beam search against a PRM degrades on easy questions and at large budgets.
agent_test: Sweep N for a model-judge selector on a held-out set and plot accuracy against N at equal token cost. Check for a peak. Compare with a code-checked selector that has no peak.

claim: A verifier with a non-zero false-positive rate puts a ceiling on resampling; weaker generators have higher false-positive rates, so more samples do not let them catch a stronger model. With a cost on false passes the best number of tries is small (sources say below 10, and about 3 or fewer in one fitted case).
agent_test: Score a draft test suite's false-positive rate against held-out tests, then cap resample count by it. Compare K=3, K=10 and K=30 against a held-out score. The direction is established by Stroebl (theory plus HumanEval+/MBPP+) and Brown (flaky and wrong tests); the exact K depends on the cost ratio and is not established. Gap search d20: Stroebl re-opened. At a false-pass cost of 4 times the benefit, optimal K is about 5 for all four models; at 10 times it is 0. No stated closed form; the marginal rule (keep sampling while P(next accepted is right) x benefit > P(next accepted is a false pass) x cost) follows from their setup. Log accept rate and audit a sample of accepted answers to estimate the false-pass rate. Gap 5 partly closed.

claim: Test suites are imperfect verifiers: 11.3% of SWE-bench Lite problems have flaky tests that can fail the gold patch, and 35 of 122 CodeContests Python3 test problems have listed correct solutions that fail the tests. Re-run checks and test the checker on known-good answers first.
agent_test: Run each check twice on a known-good answer and count disagreement; treat any disagreement as no signal. Re-read in the primary text this session.

claim: A model reviewing its own answer without external feedback does not improve reasoning and often lowers accuracy; earlier gains came from oracle labels telling it when to stop. GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 to 74.7 over two self-correct rounds (oracle labels: 84.3); GPT-4 95.5 to 89.0.
agent_test: Equal-token A/B: a self-critique pass vs one more independent sample on the same items; count right-to-wrong and wrong-to-right flips. Boundary: tested on 2023 GPT-3.5/GPT-4, not on RL-trained reasoning models. Gap search update: the direction now holds on newer models too. Qwen2.5-Math-7B intrinsic correction on MATH500 71.6 to 70.4 (d12); spontaneous mid-trace shifts in RL-trained small models are rare (6.31% of traces) and mildly harmful (d11); in Qwen3-8B traces 85 to 95% of rechecks are confirmatory (d13). Triggered reconsideration at high entropy gave +8.41 points on math (d11). Still no test on frontier reasoning models (o-series, R1 full size); gap 3 partly closed.

claim: LLM self-verification has high false-negative rates on some tasks: GPT-4 as verifier rejected 113 of 118 correct graph colourings (95.8%) and 100 of 103 correct Mystery Blocksworld plans (97.09%). A sound external verifier gives large gains; critique content adds little beyond pass/fail, and resampling matches backprompting. Counter-evidence (d04): on plan checking, Claude-3.5-Sonnet had error recall 91.85 and precision 93.74 and Gemini-1.5-Pro recall 94.04 and precision 97.51 on Trip Planning, so the rate is task- and model-specific. On math with 20 averaged checks, Gemini 1.5 Pro error rates were 7 to 23 percent (d02). o1-preview failed to flag 73% (Blocksworld) to 84% (Mystery Blocksworld) of impossible goals (d15).
agent_test: Measure the false-negative rate of our verifier step on known-correct answers per task type before enabling a reject loop. Both papers are from the same group (Stechly, Kambhampati). The Blocksworld row of the table is internally inconsistent (see critique). Gap 2 partly closed: no current-model replication of Stechly's colouring and Blocksworld rates was found, and no constraint-puzzle measurement; plan checking shows the old rate does not hold in general.

claim: Verification is not always easier than generation for LLMs: on graph colouring GPT-4 verified no better than it solved, and with itself as verifier only 1 of 100 instances ended correct. Verification gets easier when the check is a program or a reference answer.
agent_test: For each task family, compare the accuracy of our verifier step on candidates with the accuracy of solving. Route to a code check where the verifier is not clearly stronger than the solver. c19 was not re-opened this session. Gap search d04: on Trip Planning the verifier (recall 92 to 94 percent) is far better than the solver (initial accuracy 42 to 43 percent), so verification was easier than generation for planning with checkable constraints; on AIME and LiveCodeBench it was not.

claim: At practical budgets, self-consistency voting is more compute-efficient than a generative verifier with best-of-N. GenRM first matches SC only after up to 8x the compute. Optimal solutions scale as C^0.57 and verifications as C^0.39. GenRM-FT gives up to 30% relative gain over SC on the hardest MATH level (level 5, Llama-3.1-8B). Counter-evidence at the level of training-free prompted verification (d01, d03): Gemini 1.5 Pro Verification@200 beat Consistency@1000 on AIME (8/15 vs 3/15) and LiveBench Reasoning (97/140 vs 73/140), and best-of-N with self-verification beat majority vote by 10.7 points on Trip Planning (60.6 vs 49.9) and 6.9 on Meeting Planning, but lost on AIME (28.3 vs 32.2). The verification runs cost far more tokens than the voting runs in d01 (about 130M tokens per AIME question).
agent_test: At equal tokens, compare SC over S samples with fewer samples plus k verification chains, split by difficulty. Gate verification to hard items. Zhang (GenRM) reports gains against discriminative RMs and does not charge for verifier tokens, so it does not contradict Singhi. Gap 1 partly closed: verify-then-vote crosses over where voting has saturated or where the check is easier than the solve; it was not shown at equal tokens against voting at a matching N, and tie-breaking accounts for most of the gain on MATH and LiveBench Math (d01 Table 3).

claim: A generative verifier that writes a check before judging beats a scalar score and a prompted judge, and improves with more sampled checks. Reported best-of-N gains: GSM8K 73 to 93.4, MATH 28 to 44.6, with weighted voting above plain voting. ThinkPRM adds that long-CoT verification beats LLM-as-judge at equal tokens (subsets; abstract-level numbers only).
agent_test: Replace a one-shot judge with k=4 short check chains and a code aggregator. Compare at equal tokens against the single-pass judge and against SC. c13 was seen at abstract level only, and K08 limits the budget range where this pays.

claim: Process-level checks beat answer-level checks on hard math when right answers hide wrong steps. Best-of-1860 on MATH: PRM 78.2, ORM 72.4, majority 69.6. OOD STEM (234 problems, best-of-100): 72.9 / 63.8 / 61.3. On GSM8K trace error falls from 12.4% to about 3.4-5.5% with reward-model feedback while final-answer error barely changes (22.3 vs 23.5 without RM).
agent_test: Where the reasoning will be read or reused, add a step-level check on a sample of correct-answer cases and measure the rate of right-answer-wrong-reasoning. Lightman themselves say the false-positive problem is likely over-emphasised on MATH; GSM8K trace errors come from small human-annotated samples with wide intervals.

claim: Open PRMs trained on automatic (Monte Carlo) step labels generalise poorly to hard problems and lose to prompted strong models as step critics. ProcessBench F1 (GSM8K/MATH/Olympiad): Math-Shepherd-PRM-7B 47.9/29.5/24.8 vs GPT-4o 79.2/63.6/51.4 vs o1-mini 93.2/88.9/87.2. A human-label PRM800K model averages 56.5 vs 28.9 for MC Math-Shepherd labels, while best-of-8 hides the gap (64.9 vs 64.3).
agent_test: Evaluate any step-checker on first-error location, not only on final selection. Compare a prompted strong critic with k=4 votes against a cheap scorer at equal tokens.

claim: LLM judges have position bias, verbosity bias and weak math grading. With answer order swapped, GPT-4 stays consistent 65.0%, GPT-3.5 46.2%, Claude-v1 23.8%. The repetitive-list attack fooled Claude-v1 and GPT-3.5 in 91.3% of 23 cases, GPT-4 in 8.7%. Bias depends on the quality gap and varies by judge and task. Judging in both orders is a cheap fix.
agent_test: For any pairwise judge step, count verdict flips on order swap in a pilot run. Accept only order-consistent verdicts and compare accuracy with single-order at 2x judge cost. Numbers are from 2023 models and small samples, so measure our own judge model. c15 (Wang) was not re-opened.

claim: Giving a judge an independently produced reference answer cuts math grading failure sharply (14/20 default, 6/20 CoT, 3/20 reference). Having the judge solve first helps little when it copies the candidate's error.
agent_test: Compare a judge given a code-computed or independently sampled reference with a judge given none, on known right and wrong answers. The sample is 20 trials, and the reference came from the judge's own earlier answer. Gap search: d22 shows a labeler given the gold answer and step definitions holds its verdicts, while without them agreement on chains labelled correct falls to 7%. d26 shows reference-based judges reach 89 to 96% in chemistry and biology but are weaker in math. Neither tests an independently sampled reference or more than 20 trials, so gap 10 stays open.

claim: Models can recognise their own text and prefer it; self-preference tracks self-recognition (GPT-4 73.5% recognition out of the box). On correctness-checked tasks with 12 judges, the false-acceptance ratio for a judge's own failing outputs is 1.88 when it recognises them as its own vs 0.72 when it does not (LiveCodeBench), and it stays above 1 in the lowest-perplexity quartile (1.48), so familiarity alone does not explain it. A familiarity account (judges prefer low-perplexity text whoever wrote it) is weaker on these tasks. Hide authorship and prefer a judge from a different model family.
agent_test: Grade matched pairs from our own generator and from another model, blind, with equal content quality. Compare a same-family and an other-family judge. c17 was seen only as a summary; effect sizes not extracted. Gap 6 closed in direction (d16): recognition is the stronger correlate; the analysis is observational binning. A five-family majority committee cut the bias significantly for four of five members on LiveCodeBench but did not remove it (d17).

claim: Multi-agent debate does not beat self-consistency at equal responses on GSM8K (GPT-3.5): SC 85.3 at 6 and 88.2 at 9 responses vs debate 83.2 (6) and 83.0 (9).
agent_test: Equal-token comparison on our items: k independent samples with a vote vs a k-response critique round. Correction: a11 listed debate at 3 and 9 responses; the table gives 6 and 9.

claim: Verifier-guided search should be chosen by difficulty and budget. Compute-optimal allocation matched best-of-N with up to 4x less compute with oracle difficulty bins; the gain shrinks with predicted bins. Beam search wins at low budget and on hard items; best-of-N wins on easy items and at high budget.
agent_test: Route by a cheap difficulty signal (pilot agreement rate). Compare routed vs uniform strategy at equal tokens. Snell is one PaLM 2 / MATH setup; Singhi shows the same direction by different methods (GenRM helps most on level 5). Gap 9 partly closed: cheap pilot agreement works for deciding how many samples to draw (d24: 33 to 65 percent fewer calls at matched accuracy, n=50 and n=30, 3B model; d25: up to 75 percent smaller budget on GPQA, measured against the infinite-budget vote). Routing between vote, beam search and verification by pilot agreement has not been tested.

claim: Model-written tests (CodeT) raise code pass@1 (HumanEval 47.0 to 65.8) but test and code come from one model and their errors correlate, so agreement is weak independent evidence. Measured in 2026 (d18): tests written after seeing faulty code detect 14% of faults vs 25% when written independently from the task description; showing the implementation cuts fault detection by 13.2% on average across five models, and chain-of-thought and chain-of-verification prompting do not repair it. Weak-test false positives also show worse style.
agent_test: Compare generated tests, tests from the problem statement, and held-out cases on the share of selected answers that fail held-out cases. No direct measure of test-code error correlation exists in the evidence. Gap 4 mostly closed: the number is a fault-detection drop (25% to 14%), not a correlation coefficient. Write checks from the spec in a fresh context.

claim: Majority voting cannot find a rare correct answer because it picks the mode. On MATH with Llama-3-8B, coverage reached 98.44% at 10,000 samples while vote or reward model reached 41.41%.
agent_test: On hard items where the answer split is flat, escalate from voting to a code or independent check rather than adding samples.

claim: Verification matters more as test-time spend grows: verifier-based methods beat verifier-free distillation, with a gap that widens with budget (proof plus experiments at 3B, 8B, 32B).
agent_test: On long runs, reserve part of the budget for verification and compare with spending it all on generation. The evidence is about fine-tuning, so transfer to a scaffold-only agent is unproven. c23 was not re-opened.

claim: Wrong attempts carry information: V-STaR's DPO verifier trained on correct and wrong samples beat correct-only filtering (4 to 17 points on LLaMA2 7B/13B).
agent_test: Record failed attempts and their failure reasons in the scratch memory and test whether passing them to later sampling lowers repeat failures at equal tokens. V-STaR is about training, not scaffolds.

claim: Learned verification needs enough data: Cobbe found a trained verifier does not beat fine-tuning at small training sets, and the 175B verifier takes off earlier than the 6B.
agent_test: Not testable for a training-free agent; use it as a reason to prefer code checks over learned scorers.

claim: Training-free verify-then-vote beats plain voting where checking is easier than solving and where voting has plateaued, at much higher token cost. Gemini 1.5 Pro with 50 checks per candidate: AIME 8/15 vs 3/15 for Consistency@1000; best-of-N with self-verification beat majority vote on Trip Planning 60.6 vs 49.9 and Meeting Planning 55.7 vs 48.8, with SETS (add self-correction) reaching 68.5 and 59.6. On AIME verify-only lost (28.3 vs 32.2).
agent_test: Run vote-only at N versus vote at N/2 plus a pairwise check of the top two answers, at equal tokens, split by task type. Both sources are Google teams on Gemini (and Claude-3.5 in SETS); tie-breaking explains most of the gain on MATH. Not tested at truly equal tokens.

claim: Reasoning models are weak judges of whether a task is possible: o1-preview marked only 27% (Blocksworld) and 16% (Randomized Mystery Blocksworld) of unsolvable instances as unsolvable, returned a full impossible plan in 54% and 79%, and wrongly called 11.5% of solvable Mystery instances impossible.
agent_test: Keep a sound external validator (plan checker, constraint program) for planning tasks and include some unsolvable cases when auditing the verifier. 2024 model, one benchmark family.

claim: Model-based verifiers can be gamed and their static accuracy does not predict that. A trained verifier with higher static accuracy diverged from the oracle after about 450 RL steps, simple adversarial strings fooled most LLM verifiers (up to 77.9% success on one judge), and generative reasoning verifiers were more exposed than discriminative ones. RL-trained reasoning models use shortcuts that pass an instance-level checker: 458 shortcuts at complexity levels 11 to 20 vs 40 at levels 1 to 10, and gpt-5-mini shortcuts rose from 0 to 84 with more reasoning effort.
agent_test: Before accepting a pass, change the instance (rename, reorder, new inputs) and re-run the check; strip the candidate's self-assessment text before any model judge. Math and logic-rule tasks only; RL setting for most of the evidence.

claim: Using a different model family to write the tests did not lower shared error in one study: 5 LLMs on Elixir, 459 implementations and 2,709 test suites, no difference between same-model and different-model tests; 99 of 247 faulty implementations were caught only by hand-written tests.
agent_test: Test isolation of context (spec only) against isolation of model family at equal budget on held-out cases. Rare language, so all models may share blind spots.

claim: Step-level scoring does not transfer outside its training domain: math PRMs add at most +0.71 points over majority voting across non-math MMLU-Pro subjects (Philosophy +0.34, History +0.20) vs +4.80 on math, while a multi-domain PRM got +7.9% in Law. An LLM step labeler without a reference answer and step definitions agreed with its own earlier correct labels only 7% of the time.
agent_test: Use step-level checks only where a labelled calibration set exists for the domain; otherwise spend on answer-level independent checks. MMLU-Pro multiple choice, machine labels; the value of step-level over answer-level checking outside math is still not isolated (gap 7 open).

claim: Ensembles of diverse imperfect verifiers beat voting only when weighted by estimated accuracy: Weaver 87.7 average vs majority vote 72.2 and naive top-10 reward-model ensemble 69.1 (Llama 3.3 70B, K=100, 33 verifiers). It needs a small labelled dev set (naive threshold 79.0 vs 87.5 with 5% labels), and dropping verifiers that are always positive or always negative gives 79.4 to 85.2. Gains flatten from correlated bias on hard items; score correlation between verifiers was only about 0.03.
agent_test: Run 3 to 5 different checks (code run, constraint script, different-family judge, pairwise compare), measure each on a labelled set of 30 to 100 items, and weight or drop by measured accuracy. Paper has internal numeric inconsistencies; verifiers are trained reward models, not prompts.

claim: Majority voting errors were not positively correlated in an olympiad setting, so prompt diversity cannot reduce them: all 19 pairwise-correlation estimates were negative (mean -0.348; mean -0.122 for N of 7 or more), diversity lowered the score monotonically, and the gap between best majority vote (42/50) and pass@20 (45.5) is selection loss.
agent_test: Do not spend budget on prompt diversity for voters; test a selector over the vote instead. Estimate is on correct-vote counts and noisy; 50 problems; no verifier tested.

claim: Spontaneous self-verification by RL-trained reasoning models rarely finds errors. Mid-trace shifts occur in 6.31% of traces and are mildly harmful on math and crosswords; 85 to 95% of rechecks in Qwen3-8B are confirmatory; but a forced reconsideration cue when entropy is high lifted math accuracy from 32.2% to 40.6%. Hidden states carry a correctness signal (AUC above 0.7, above 0.9 on AIME at 32B) that the model does not use.
agent_test: Trigger a second look only on a measured uncertainty signal (vote disagreement), not by default; compare to one more sample at equal tokens. Evidence is from small and mid models (1.5B to 32B); no test on frontier reasoning models.

claim: Cheap agreement among a few pilot samples is a usable difficulty signal for allocating samples: stopping early when 2 to 4 samples agree matched fixed self-consistency with 33 to 65 percent fewer calls (3B model, n=50 and n=30), and adaptive allocation reached the infinite-budget vote on GPQA with up to 75 percent (offline) and 55 percent (online) less budget.
agent_test: Pilot 3 samples; stop on agreement, add up to the cap on disagreement; compare to uniform at equal tokens. Weak: small n, small model, and PETS measures agreement with the vote, not truth.

claim: Pairwise self-verification (which of two candidates is right) is more accurate than scoring each alone: a training-free tournament that spends comparisons on the least certain pairs raised Pass@1 by up to 10% over pointwise verification on code and math; separate evidence shows scoring each candidate alone is miscalibrated and that more samples make verification easier.
agent_test: As the verification step, compare the top two voted answers pairwise with a short check instead of scoring each. Only abstract and intro of V1 were read.
